Keeping peptides cool in Mesa

Mesa's reference station is NOAA's East Mesa site, at about 1,518 feet and roughly 4.3 miles east-northeast of the city's Census center point.76 Its 1991 to 2020 normals, based on about 15 to 16 years of records, give July a 105.9 °F high and a 78.9 °F low, and January a 67.5 °F high and a 41.0 °F low.7 In an average year the station records 112.1 days at or above 100 °F, 176.5 days at or above 90 °F and 11.1 nights at or below freezing, with 10.76 inches of precipitation.1

Summer days run about as hot as central Phoenix, where Sky Harbor's July normal high is 106.5 °F.8 Winter nights run colder: East Mesa's January low is 5 °F below Sky Harbor's 46.0 °F.78

Approved medicines show why no single storage rule fits every freeze-dried product. Under their FDA labels, EGRIFTA SV (tesamorelin) vials are kept at room temperature (20 to 25 °C), ZOMACTON (somatropin) vials in a refrigerator (2 to 8 °C), and one chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) product at 20 to 25 °C.9105 EGRIFTA SV permits excursions only from 15 to 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), and that is one product's tested limit, not a rule for any other peptide.9 A Mesa afternoon from June to August averages 104.9 °F,1 well past that range. The practical rule: bring the parcel indoors as soon as it arrives and store each vial as its label or product page directs. The storage guide goes further.

About Mesa

Mormon colonists from Utah and Idaho reached the Salt River Valley on February 14, 1878, and used an abandoned Hohokam canal for part of their first irrigation project.11 The town of Mesa City incorporated on July 15, 1883.11 Most of the growth came after 1950: nearly 17,000 people lived on just over 6 square miles in 1950, and 396,375 on 125 square miles by 2000.11 The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 513,656 residents, on 142.1 square miles of land.126

Aerospace runs through the city's history. Falcon Field opened in 1941 to train British pilots, and Williams Field, built the same year for American pilots, served as an Air Force training base until 1993 before reopening as an airport, now Phoenix-Mesa Gateway.11 Hughes Helicopter opened its Apache helicopter factory in Mesa in 1982, a plant later run by McDonnell Douglas and then Boeing.11 In the city's employer table, Boeing has 4,600 Mesa-based jobs, behind Mesa Public Schools (7,829), Banner Health (6,468) and the City of Mesa (5,250).13

The city's health and science base includes Banner Health, its second-largest employer, and Dexcom, with 1,867 Mesa-based staff.13 ASU's 600-acre Polytechnic campus, established in 1996, enrolls 4,782 undergraduate and 1,388 graduate and professional students; its colleges include the College of Health Solutions, and its labs include semiconductor fabrication labs.2 A.T. Still University's School of Osteopathic Medicine in Arizona also lists a Mesa address.14 Landmarks include the Arizona Temple, dedicated on October 23, 1927, and the Mesa Arts Center, opened downtown in 2005.11

Nearby

Mesa's center lies about 17 miles east of the Phoenix Sky Harbor weather station, and METRO light rail has linked Mesa with Tempe and Phoenix since December 2008.6811 All of the county's pages start from Peptides in Phoenix. Pages also cover Tempe, Gilbert, Chandler and Fountain Hills, and the full list is on the locations page.

Frequently asked questions

Do you ship HCG to Mesa?

Yes. HCG is sold as a 5000 IU vial and ships to any Mesa address under the same shipping policy as orders across the United States. Its product page shows the price and the stock for each ship-from origin before checkout, since stock can differ between origins. Like everything in the catalog, it is sold for laboratory research only, as the research use policy explains.

Mesa is a large city. Is there a D2C Peptides location there?

No. ASU calls Mesa Arizona's third-largest city,2 but D2C Peptides lists no location there or anywhere else in Maricopa County, which is why this page shows no address or map. Mesa orders are handled by shipping only. Questions before or after an order go to the contact page, and the county's pages are all linked from Peptides in Phoenix.

How warm can an HCG vial get before it is a problem?

What heat a specific research peptide can tolerate, HCG included, has not been published, so the storage condition on its label or product page is the guide.34 For comparison, the label of one FDA-approved chorionic gonadotropin product says to store the unmixed vial at 20 to 25 °C (68 to 77 °F).5 East Mesa's June to August normal high is 104.9 °F,1 far above that range, so a delivered parcel should come indoors promptly.

Where is the certificate of analysis for my HCG vial?

The lab results page lists lab documents, including certificates of analysis, by product and lot number as they become available. Match the lot number on your vial's label to a listed document. If your lot is not listed, write to us through the contact page with the product, strength and lot number before using the vial in a study, so that any mix-up can be checked while the vial is still sealed. The returns page covers wrong or damaged items.
